record.paper_title: Open Problems in Understanding the Nuclear Chirality
record.context_brief: Unified model of chiral vibration and static chirality
record.original_question: What theoretical framework can simultaneously describe the precursor regime of chiral vibration, the static-chirality regime produced by quantum tunneling between left-handed and right-handed configurations, and the smooth evolution between those two regimes within one unified treatment of nuclear chirality?

evidence.quote: Further investigation in a more microscopic way is expected. In particular, we need a model which could simultaneously describe the chiral
vibration dominated by a slow vibration, static chirality by the quantum tunneling, and the smooth transition from chiral vibration to static chirality.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
In the study of rotational bands of triaxially deformed atomic nuclei, "nuclear chirality" arises when the angular momentum vectors of the core and of valence nucleons (a particle and a hole, say) lie along three mutually perpendicular axes of the triaxial intrinsic shape, so that the total angular momentum has a nonzero component out of any principal plane. This produces two intrinsic configurations related by an improper rotation — a left-handed and a right-handed configuration — that, in the laboratory frame, give rise to a pair of nearly degenerate ΔI = 1 rotational bands.

Two qualitatively different physical regimes are recognized:

(a) Chiral-vibration regime: the system performs slow, large-amplitude vibrations of the angular-momentum vectors through the planar (achiral) configuration; the two partner bands appear as zero- and one-phonon states of this vibration, and inter-band electromagnetic matrix elements show a characteristic pattern (e.g., M1/E2 staggering and selection rules consistent with a soft chiral mode).

(b) Static-chirality regime: the chiral geometry is well established in the intrinsic frame, the two partner bands correspond to the symmetric and antisymmetric linear combinations of the left-handed and right-handed configurations, and their energy splitting is governed by quantum tunneling between these two configurations.

Construct a single theoretical/microscopic framework (for example, based on a triaxial particle-rotor model, cranking plus collective Hamiltonian, generator-coordinate method, or interacting-boson-fermion-fermion model, etc.) that

1. reproduces the precursor (chiral-vibration) regime, including the soft-mode behavior of the angular-momentum geometry and the resulting energies and electromagnetic transition probabilities of the partner bands;

2. reproduces the static-chirality regime, in which the energy splitting of the partner bands is described as the result of quantum tunneling between the left-handed and right-handed configurations, with the corresponding electromagnetic selection rules; and

3. yields a smooth, parameter-controlled evolution between regime (a) and regime (b) as functions of spin, deformation, and single-particle configuration, without requiring a separate model for each regime.

Specify the framework explicitly, derive the energies and B(M1)/B(E2) values of the chiral-partner bands as functions of spin within it, and demonstrate analytically or numerically the smooth crossover between the vibrational and the tunneling-dominated regimes.
artifact.status_search_result: Searches turned up individual studies of chiral vibration vs. static chirality (e.g., the 135Nd Phys. Rev. Lett. 99, 172501 (2007) and more recent 2024 work on chirality evolution from transverse wobbling), but no single microscopic framework that has been broadly accepted as simultaneously describing the chiral-vibration regime, the static-chirality regime via tunneling, and the smooth crossover between them. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: From Chiral Vibration to Static Chirality in 135Nd
status_evidence.snippet: Behavior of partner bands associated with a transition from a vibrational into a static chiral regime.
status_evidence.claim: Empirical evidence of the two regimes exists, motivating but not providing a unified microscopic model.

status_evidence.title: Nuclear Theory listings, March 2024 (arXiv)
status_evidence.snippet: Evolution of chirality from transverse wobbling in 135Pr.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work continues to explore evolution of nuclear chirality, indicating no unified framework has settled the question.
